observation.visible_scene: A KÄRCHER-branded steam mop (dark grey/black rectangular head with a white microfiber pad, mounted on a vertical brown handle with a small yellow clip/button) is being worked across a glossy beige ceramic-tile floor with visible grout lines. A bright window reflection appears on the left tile, and a wet, sheen-covered strip marks the cleaned surface. The KÄRCHER logo sits as a fixed overlay in the top-right corner throughout.
visible_changes: The mop head translates from a low, near position in the frame (frames 1–5) up toward the top edge, partly cropped out (frames 16–22), then back down to a low, near position (frames 30–41) — i.e. a pull-away-then-return motion of the tool relative to the camera.
The handle and its yellow accent move together with the head, confirming the whole tool is shifting rather than just the head rotating.
A visible steam/vapor plume rises around the head, most prominent in the early-to-mid frames and noticeably reduced or absent in the later frames.
The wet glossy cleaned strip on the tiles changes shape and extent as the head moves across it.
The head's orientation shifts slightly (swivel joint), appearing more tilted in some mid frames and squared in others.
outside_clip_unknowns: Who operates the mop and the steam-generating machine body are not shown.
The state of the floor before cleaning and any outcome after the excerpt are unknown.
Whether the back-and-forth motion continues beyond the last frame is not shown.
uncertain_details: The apparent vertical travel could be partly due to camera tilt/pan rather than pure mop translation; background reflection and grout positions shift only modestly, so camera motion is uncertain.
Whether the steam plume genuinely diminishes or merely becomes less visible due to angle is unclear.
The exact 3D direction of the mop relative to an unseen operator cannot be determined from the framing alone.
